AI read

The board leans bear and the bar for action is met, so this is a ACT rung read rather than a watch. The weight is in the risk-off cluster: SKEW tail pricing, dealer gamma, high-yield spreads, HYG drawdown, the haven filter, and three separate breadth jaws (NDX vs NYSE, FANG+ vs the rest, Dow Theory transports) are all on alert together, which is the kind of stack you don't get in a healthy market.

One step behind that, the JPY haven cluster, credit-SPX correlation, VIX9D inversion, and loose financial conditions are the closest to firing, so the next shoe is more likely to drop than to pull back. The session moved the needle further bear: SPTM composite vs VIX jaws came on alert and PMO breadth entered the buy-zone build, while VIX9D front inversion, the topping composite divergence, and the VIX-backwardation-x-credit pair dropped off, a mixed shuffle that still leaves the net alert count higher.

To turn this from a lean into a trade, you want one of the closest-to-firing set (JPY cluster or credit-SPX correlation is the cleanest) to actually trip, and the kill is simple: HYG repairs, SKEW cools, and the breadth jaws close, in which case the ACT rung was a head-fake and you stand down.

Confluence over 8 weeks bear vs bull
Four rungs, and you only act on the top one. STAND DOWN, nothing is on. WATCH, one or two signals are true but they stand alone. SETUP, several are lining up. ACT, three of them have held for three sessions and they come from three different families, so it is not the same idea counted three times. A signal only counts once it has held three sessions, because one day in the zone is noise. Signals our lab rejected are left out of the count.
The three counts: firing = the condition is true at today's close, confirmed = it has been true 3 sessions in a row (this is what the bar counts), building = not true yet but close.
How to read each row: every signal is a checklist. Most of them need several things to be true at the same moment, so each line shows the condition, where it stands now and what it needs. A signal fires only when every box is ticked, which is why a number can sit well past its own trigger while the row still reads BUILDING. Some signals have two paths, either one arms them. ALERT (red bear / green bull) = it just fired, BUILDING = getting close, QUIET = nothing here yet. Widening? tells you whether the divergence is still growing or easing back. Statuses recompute nightly from the EOD pipeline. Confirmed = 3 consecutive sessions in zone (the framework buffer rule: one day in zone is noise). In formation = consecutive sessions spent in the top quintile of the metric. Sources: Polygon cache, nightly signal history tables, Yahoo for index series, FRED for macro.
